Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood MAP & Integration next steps

Great — thanks for confirming owners, Sarah. Per Mark's question, attaching a short technical note below and including a proposed owner breakdown in the MAP (see attachments).

Technical notes (summary):
- SDK integration: Redwood provides a TypeScript SDK and a lightweight Python client. SDKs support streaming responses natively; we recommend using our streaming client for low-latency UX (example code in SDK docs).
- Streaming & session stickiness: for multi-turn flows we use a connection-scoped session ID or token to maintain KV cache affinity. If you want strict session placement we can enable session pinning to a dedicated pool (requires Dedicated or private deployment).
- Prefix/KV caching: Redwood does automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts; we expose cache controls so you can opt-in to stronger cache reuse across similar requests.
- Tool calling / structured outputs: we suggest a top-level JSON schema (intent, entities, tool_invocations[]) — attached is an example schema and sample webhook payload.

Milestone owner breakdown (in MAP draft):
- SDK integration (TypeScript + Python): Owner: Mark Reed (Acme) / Redwood SE (Marissa) — tasks: SDK hookup, auth flow, unit tests
- Streaming integration & validation: Owner: Mark Reed (Acme) / Redwood Eng (Vivek) — tasks: session handling, latency testing, test harness
- Tool calling + structured outputs: Owner: Acme Backend (Mark) / Redwood SE (Stephanie) — tasks: schema sign-off, contract tests, webhook config
- Pilot run & acceptance: Owner: Acme Product (Sarah) / Redwood Customer Success

Next steps: I'll update the MAP to call out the owners and include the sample schema by Monday. Can Mark confirm which infra env (dev/staging) he'll want Redwood to push test keys to?

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachments referenced: ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf, integration_build_plan_sketch.xlsx
